title: Boolean Logic‐Assisted Organic Photoelectrochemical Transistor DNA Molecular Computing Platform for Dual‐miRNA‐Based Precise Breast Cancer Diagnosis
abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐biomarker OPECT biosensing is prone to false positives, and although Boolean logic gates improve specificity through dual‐target triggering, they typically sacrifice sensitivity or depend on fragmented, multi‐step readouts. Herein, we report an OPECT‐based DNA molecular‐computing platform that reframes biosensing as a programmable Boolean‐responsive trigger (BRT) circuits with a rationally engineered Cu‐T 4 EPE/MSN@CsPbBr 3 (Cu‐T/MSN@CPB) photoelectric heterojunction for breast‐cancer detection. Halide perovskites offer exceptional carrier transport and photoelectric conversion, yet have been excluded from OPECT biosensing by aqueous instability or the lack of a continuous, biocompatible charge‐transport interface. We therefore pre‐encapsulate CsPbBr 3 quantum dots in mesoporous silica nanospheres and interface them with a porous, visible‐light‐absorbing Cu‐T MOF, forming a Cu‐T/MSN@CPB type‐II heterojunction whose matched band alignment drives directional spatial separation of photogenerated carriers, delivering a 4‐fold photocurrent response over pristine Cu‐T with stability retained in physiological buffer. On this gate, Boolean‐responsive trigger circuitry outputs a HCR‐amplified signal only when miR‐21 and miR‐31 coexist and attains detection limits of 0.13 fM (miR‐31) and 0.09 fM (miR‐21). This DNA‐encoded logic is rewirable to other cancer types, pointing toward programmable, point‐of‐care precision cancer diagnosis.

title: Pulsed Electrosynthesis of Conformal High‐Entropy Metallic Glass Skins for Durable Industrial Water Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐entropy metallic glasses (HEMGs) combine compositional diversity with a grain‐boundary‐free amorphous topology, making them attractive as electrocatalytic interfaces. However, their synthesis remains challenging because multicomponent transition‐metal alloys favor crystallization over vitrification. Here, we report a room‐temperature pulsed electrosynthesis (PES) strategy that kinetically traps HEMG skins, defined here as continuous, conformal HEMG coatings approximately 100 nm thick, directly on practical electrodes under ambient aqueous conditions. Using crystallization‐prone FeCoNiMo, millisecond ultrahigh‐current pulses induce burst multimetal nucleation while suppressing diffusion‐mediated crystallization, enabling programmable control over crystallinity, morphology, and composition. The resulting chemically homogeneous, grain‐boundary‐free skins suppress localized corrosion and structural collapse, favoring spatially distributed surface reconstruction. FeCoNiMo HEMG‐skinned electrodes sustain alkaline hydrogen evolution at 2 A cm −2 for over 1,300 h, whereas crystalline counterparts fail within approximately 200 h. As bifunctional electrodes in an anion‐exchange‐membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE), they achieve 1 A cm −2 at 1.706 V and operate for 1,200 h, outperforming the Pt/C‖IrO 2 benchmark under identical conditions. Roll‐to‐roll upgrading of commercial Ni mesh (0.5 m × 2 m) further demonstrates fabrication scalability. These results establish PES‐driven HEMG skinning as a practical route for integrating metastable amorphous multimetal interfaces with electrode architectures.

title: Bimodal Pore Engineering of Mesoporous Carbon onto Ti3C2T x via a Soft–Hard Templating Route for Highly Durable Potassium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional mesoporous carbon materials with tailored porosity and robust interfacial coupling are pivotal for potassium-ion batteries, yet the precise construction of bimodal pores remains a critical bottleneck. Herein, we propose an interfacial assembly strategy for the in situ growth of N,P-co-doped bimodal mesoporous carbon onto Ti3C2Tx MXene (D-NMC/Ti3C2Tx) via a phytic acid (PA)-mediated soft–hard dual-templating route. Both theoretical and experimental results demonstrate that PA serves as a molecular bridge, reinforcing hydrogen-bonding interactions to orchestrate the coassembly of P123, SiO2 nanospheres, and 2,6-diaminopyridine onto the functionalized Ti3C2Tx surface. Attributed to the unique design, D-NMC/Ti3C2Tx delivers a high reversible capacity of 303.6 mAh g–1 at 0.1 A g–1 over 200 cycles and retains 148.3 mAh g–1 after 3500 cycles at 1.0 A g–1. XPS depth profiling reveals that the enhanced performance originates from a stable inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase that maintains electrode integrity. This work offers a promising strategy for designing advanced carbon-based electrodes.

title: Enantioselective Access to Bis‐U‐Shaped Hexapyrrolic Expanded Porphyrinoids via a BINAM‐Directed Axial‐to‐Helical Chirality Transfer Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral expanded porphyrinoids hold great promise for chiroptical applications, while stereospecific access to enantiopure expanded porphyrinoids remains a significant challenge due to their conformational heterogeneity, tedious post‐synthetic resolution, and poor configurational stability. Herein, we employ 1,1'‐binaphthyl‐2,2'‐diamine (BINAM) as both the core building block and chiral directing group for the one‐pot stereospecific synthesis of a ‘ bis‐U‐shaped ’ hexapyrrolic expanded porphyrinoid platform. The axially chiral twisted conformation of BINAM imposes a strong conformational constraint during cyclization with tripyrrin subunits, inducing synchronous helical twisting of the conjugated chains and establishing multiple stereogenic helical elements. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction confirms quantitative transfer of BINAM axial chirality to persistent macrocyclic P / M helicity, affording enantiomers with exceptional thermal stability (no racemization even at 180°C). Notably, both Zn(II) and Co(II) bind via an unprecedented cross‐bridging mode, chelating dipyrrin donors from two separate tripyrrin units rather than undergoing conventional central insertion. This coordination rigidifies the folded framework, amplifies the chiroptical response (|g abs | values from 0.0096 to 0.0126 and 0.0137 for Zn(II) and Co(II) complexes, respectively), and directs homochiral supramolecular self‐assembly into one‐dimensional helical nanostructures in the solid state.

title: Origin of Enhanced Mass Transfer in Electrochemical Reactions Boosted by Hierarchically Porous Metal–Organic Framework Thin Films
abstract: Abstract Zirconium-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have been used in various electrochemical applications owing to their chemical robustness in aqueous solutions, and MOF thin films on electrodes can sometimes boost the electrochemical response of a reaction occurring on the underlying electrode, even though the MOF is not electrically conductive. Herein, the origin of the enhanced electrochemical response caused by such porous and inert MOF coatings with diverse pore sizes is investigated. Electrochemically inactive zirconium-based MOFs with large mesopores, small mesopores, and no mesopores are synthesized by employing soft-template-assisted synthesis, and membrane-type thick MOF coatings are deposited on electrodes to study the electrochemical reactions of redox probes coming from the external electrolyte. Ferrocyanide(II) and hexaammine-ruthenium(III) are selected as redox probes, and electrochemical studies are performed at various concentrations. The effect of the MOF coating on the diffusion coefficient of the redox probe and the preconcentration of the redox probe caused by the MOF coating, are investigated separately by electroanalytical techniques. Results suggest that MOF overlayers can largely amplify the electrochemical responses of both redox probes at low concentrations, and such enhancements are mainly attributed to the preconcentration of redox-active ions caused by the MOF, rather than the difference in diffusion coefficient; mesopores created in MOF thin films only marginally increase the diffuse coefficient of redox probes. Such stable MOF coatings are thus desirable to generate amplified electrochemical responses in electroanalytic and electrocatalytic systems with low concentrations of ionic reactants.

title: Fully Conjugated Chiral Covalent Organic Frameworks Enabling High‐Density Polaron Hopping Conduction via Spin‐Frustration Relief
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic semiconductors are key materials for high‐performance organic electronics, where both high carrier density and fast carrier mobility are required to achieve high conductivity. However, increasing carrier concentrations inevitably introduces scattering effect that severely impair charge transport. Here we report a strategy to synthesize highly polarized covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through chirality‐induced crystallization and a subsequent COF‐to‐COF transformation, yielding benzothiazole‐linked fully conjugated frameworks. The resulting porous organic crystals feature an enhanced polarization arising from the parallel stacking of benzothiazole moieties, which enables precise N‐over‐N and S‐over‐S atomic alignment across neighboring layers. Benefiting from anisotropic polarization, the chiral COF film exhibits an excellent intrinsic conductivity of 1.9 × 10 −2 S cm −1 , along with a high carrier concentration of 1.1 × 10 17 cm −3 and a fast carrier mobility of 1.1 cm 2 V −1 s −1 . Upon iodine doping, the optimal conductivity of the chiral COFs is enhanced by more than one order of magnitude compared to that of the achiral analog with antiparallel stacking. We provide insights into the polaron‐mediated conduction mechanism through electron‐phonon coupling in the axisymmetric polarized frameworks, which addresses the carrier‐scattering issue even at high carrier densities. Our findings establish highly polarized organic crystals as promising semiconductors for advanced electronics.

title: Through‐Space Hot‐Electron Transfer Between Gold Nanoclusters and MOF Boosting Photothermal Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT The structural elucidation of metal nanocluster@MOF composites remains challenging due to their poor crystallinity, hindering the establishment of precise structure–property relationships. Here, we present a reverse templating strategy in which atomically precise gold nanoclusters (GNCs) to direct MOF crystallization, yielding highly crystalline GNC@MOF single crystals for single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction (SCXRD) analysis. Coarse‐grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations reveal the adaptive growth of MOFs around spherical GNC template, accompanied by a complete topological transformation from rectangular to hexagonal symmetry. Combining transient absorption spectroscopy, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and optoelectronic measurements, we reveals pronounced space interfacial electron coupling between GNCs and MOFs. This coupling facilitates directional transfer of photoexcited hot electrons from GNCs to MOFs, resulting in enhanced photothermal conversion performance. Upon 660 nm laser irradiation, Au 13 @Zn‐NDC‐MOF rapidly heats to 106.3°C within 6 s and reaches a maximum temperature of 182.0°C (∆ T = 158.1°C), outperforming discrete Au 13 clusters (∆ T = 126.3°C) under identical conditions. Au 13 @Zn‐NDC‐MOF also exhibits excellent photostability over multiple on‐off cycles. This work establishes a direct link among through‐space interfacial electron coupling, hot‐electron transfer, and enhanced photothermal behavior, providing a generalizable platform for the rational design of high‐performance MNC@MOF materials for solar energy conversion and photocatalysis.

title: Self‐Assembly and Thermally Activated Bowl Inversion of Tetrabenzocorannulene Buckybowls on Ag(111)
abstract: ABSTRACT Bowl‐shaped π‐conjugated molecules possess a unique structural degree of freedom absent from planar nanographenes: bowl inversion. Understanding how this inversion couples to surface adsorption is essential for controlling the structure and function of curved molecular architectures. Here we show that the conformation of tetrabenzocorannulene (TBC) on Ag(111) is determined by the competition between intermolecular packing and molecule‐substrate interactions. By tuning the annealing temperature and duration, we induce transitions between self‐assembled phases dominated by concave‐face‐up and concave‐face‐down conformations. Scanning tunneling microscopy combined with density functional theory reveals that these phases are stabilized by different interaction regimes, with intermolecular interactions favoring concave‐face‐up structures and stronger substrate bonding stabilizing concave‐face‐down configurations. Our results establish molecular curvature as a thermodynamically tunable degree of freedom in surface‐supported molecular assemblies, providing a general strategy for controlling the structure of curved π‐conjugated nanocarbons.

title: Topology-Based Generation of Hypothetical Metal−Organic Frameworks through Single-Metal Nodes and Symmetry-Aware Linker Rotation
abstract: Abstract Topology-based hypothetical metal−organic framework (MOF) generators enable scalable exploration of chemical space beyond experimentally reported structures, but their accessible design space is constrained by the building blocks and assembly rules they encode. Here, we present PORMAKE2, an upgraded topology-based hypothetical MOF generator designed to improve both access to small-pore structures and geometric fidelity. PORMAKE2 introduces an expanded building-block library, including single-metal nodes, and implements symmetry-aware linker rotation for higher-fidelity framework assembly. These upgrades substantially expand the accessible small-pore MOF space and enable MOF designs that were inaccessible to earlier workflows, including ZIF-type and CALF-20-like structures with improved geometrical agreement. Carbon dioxide direct air capture (DAC) and xenon/krypton separation are included as case studies demonstrating that an improved framework-generation workflow can influence downstream screening outcomes. These results establish PORMAKE2 as a more expressive and chemically faithful front-end platform for hypothetical MOF generation.

title: Diatom‐Inspired Hierarchical Macro‐Mesoporous AuPd/ZnO with Topology‑Induced Metal‐Support Interactions for Ultrasensitive Monitoring of Bacterial Volatile Biomarkers
abstract: ABSTRACT Inspired by the hierarchical porous architecture of diatom frustules, we report a biomimetic hierarchically ordered macroporous mesoporous AuPd/ZnO composite as a high‐performance sensing platform for trace detection of 3 ‐hydroxy‐2‐butanone (3H2B), a critical volatile biomarker of Listeria monocytogenes. Here, the deliberate design of high curvature mesopores as topological traps to anchor AuPd nanocrystals, proposing a topology‐induced metal‐support interaction mechanism that triggers interfacial electronic restructuring. This confinement‐driven modulation optimizes oxygen reactivity and reduces the reaction energy barrier, enabling MEMS sensor with an ultralow detection limit of 9.7 ppb and high response (R a /R g = 74.4) to 10 ppm 3H2B at 150°C, significantly outperforming conventional porous materials. In situ spectroscopy and DFT calculations reveal that Pd sites within the AuPd alloy serve as primary electron donors, facilitating 3H2B dehydrogenation and oxidation. Furthermore, a portable wireless module integrated with a random forest algorithm allows accurate identification of 3H2B in complex mixtures, validating real‐time monitoring of bacterial growth in food. This work not only establishes a paradigm for precision synthesis of hierarchically porous materials but also provides profound insights into interfacial science by leveraging topological confinement to tailor electronic structures for interfacial catalytic performance and food safety applications.

title: Directional Nitrite Spillover Couples to Interfacial Hydrogen-Bond Networks for Ampere-Level Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia is often constrained by the proton-coupled hydrogenation of adsorbed nitrite (*NO2), a step commonly accelerated through hydrogen spillover and local reactive-hydrogen (*H) supply. This hydrogen-centered view, however, treats *NO2 largely as a passive intermediate and overlooks whether its migration can reconstruct the interfacial hydrogen-bond-network environment required for downstream hydrogenation. Here, we show that directional *NO2 spillover couples site-specific intermediate transport with interfacial hydrogen-bond-network reorganization. In a Cu–Ag dual-site model interface, nitrate activation and *NO2 formation occur preferentially on the Cu sites, whereas migrated *NO2 species are stabilized and hydrogenated on the Ag-associated sites. In situ spectroscopy, kinetic isotope measurements, distribution-of-relaxation-time analysis, and theoretical simulations reveal that this Cu-to-Ag relay enriches K+-associated interfacial water, reinforces hydrogen-bond connectivity, and facilitates *H delivery for *NO2 hydrogenation. The optimized CuAg N-doped carbon (CuAg–N-C) achieves near-unity Faradaic efficiency (FE) for NH3 with a yield rate of 411.8 mmol g–1 h–1 and retains 83% FE at 1 A cm–2 in a flow cell. The catalyst further retains substantial nitrate-to-ammonia recovery in simulated and authentic industrial water matrices. More broadly, this work establishes *NO2 spillover as a dynamic interfacial mechanism linking intermediate transport, water-network organization, and proton-coupled nitrogen conversion, providing a framework for sustaining molecular-scale selectivity under chemically complex reaction environments.

title: Site-Selective and Deuterium-Programmable Electrochemical Synthesis of Deuterated Pharmaceuticals
abstract: Abstract Deuterium labeling plays a pivotal role in pharmaceutical development by modulating physicochemical properties and enabling metabolic tracing. However, site-selective and programmable deuteration in amine-containing pharmaceuticals remains a formidable challenge, as it typically requires prefunctionalized and costly deuterated reagents that hamper scalability and practical utility. Here, we report an electrochemical strategy for synthesizing deuterated amine pharmaceuticals using D2O as a cost-effective deuterium source, enabling site selectivity, degree-programmable deuteration, and excellent deuterium incorporation. Central to this approach is the electrochemical conversion of toxic polyhalides into reactive deuterated building blocks in situ, facilitating the efficient synthesis of over 70 deuterated drugs, with selective mono-, di-, and trideuteration at the N-benzyl, N-methyl, O-benzyl, and S-benzyl positions, and broad functional-group tolerance. Collectively, we establish a platform integrating polyhalides valorization with precision isotopic editing for accessing high-value deuterated pharmaceuticals, especially amine-containing drugs bearing common metabolic soft spots such as benzyl and methyl motifs.

title: From Sintering to Mineralization: A Liquid-Phase Growth Route for Ceramic Films
abstract: Abstract The fabrication of dense ceramic films for solid-state electronics and energy-conversion systems has long been hindered by a fundamental sintering dilemma: the high temperatures required to activate solid-state diffusion simultaneously promote elemental volatilization, interfacial reactions, and phase segregation. Inspired by natural mineralization, we develop a biomimetic liquid-phase growth (LPG) strategy that enables the direct formation of dense ceramic films under mild conditions. As a stringent model system, we select the highly refractory proton conductor BaZr0.85Y0.15O3−δ (BZY), which possesses a melting point of 2700 °C. In the LPG process, molten Ba(NO3)2 serves as both a reactive precursor and a liquid transport medium, while a (ZrO2)0.92(Y2O3)0.08 (YSZ) seed layer confines nucleation and directs interfacial crystal growth and coalescence. This strategy produces dense, chemically homogeneous BZY films at 600 °C, more than 1000 °C below those required in conventional solid-state sintering. The evolution mechanism of the LPG process is elucidated through in situ real-time characterizations. The versatility of this strategy is further demonstrated by the successful growth of BaHfO3, BaHfO3@BZY heterostructured, and SrZr0.85Y0.15O3−δ films. Fuel-cell tests validate the electrochemical functionality of the BZY-LPG electrolytes. By reconceptualizing film densification as a liquid-phase mineralization process, LPG establishes a distinct chemical framework for the low-temperature synthesis of dense films, substantially expanding the design landscape for advanced ceramic devices.

title: Molecular Bridging Flexibility Enables Closed‐Pore Engineering in Hard Carbon for Enhanced Plateau Sodium Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Closed pores are critical structural motifs that enable low‐voltage plateau capacity in hard carbon (HC) anodes for sodium‐ion batteries, yet their controllable construction through precursor molecular design remains challenging. Herein, we demonstrate molecular bridging flexibility as an effective design principle for regulating closed‐pore formation in HCs. The flexibility/rigidity of polymer precursors is tailored by distinct bridging configurations, namely Ar─CH 2 ─Ar and Ar─O─C bridges, where oxygen‐containing bridges enhance segmental flexibility. During early‐stage pyrolysis, flexible precursor segments provide higher conformational freedom, inducing curved carbon skeletons and promoting the formation of semi‐open sub‐1 nm pores. Driven by high surface energy, these semi‐open pores undergo pore‐mouth closure during high‐temperature pyrolysis, generating abundant closed pores. The resulting HC exhibits a closed porosity of 0.12 cm 3 g −1 and a pore size 1.13 nm, which enhances plateau capacity and sodium‐ion diffusion kinetics. Consequently, the flexible‐precursor‐derived HC delivers a high reversible capacity of 356.1 mAh g −1 and a plateau capacity of 242.7 mAh g −1 . Moreover, a practical 1.2 Ah pouch cell achieves 217.2 Wh kg −1 and retains 81.2% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. This work establishes a molecular‐level strategy for closed‐pore engineering in HC anodes for high‐performance sodium‐ion batteries.

title: Advances in Donor–Acceptor Covalent Organic Frameworks: From Rational Design to Multifunctional Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Donor–acceptor (D‐A) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) provide modular crystalline platforms in which D‐A pairing, linkage chemistry, pore environments, and framework ordering can be rationally engineered to regulate light harvesting, exciton dissociation, charge separation, and charge transport. This review summarizes recent progress in the design and multifunctional applications of D‐A COFs across key linkage families, including imine, β‐ketoenamine, triazine, vinylene, boroxine, amide, ester, and hydrazone frameworks. We first discuss key structural design principles, including donor/acceptor selection, topology and linkage engineering, π‐π stacking, framework planarity, pore functionalization, and post‐synthetic modification, and relate these features to optoelectronic descriptors such as absorption/emission behavior, energy‐level alignment, and charge‐transfer dynamics. Representative applications are then organized across solar‐driven catalysis, including hydrogen evolution reaction, oxygen evolution reaction, CO 2 reduction, coupled CO–H 2 O 2 generation, as well as sensing/biosensing, biomedical phototherapies, and broadband photodetection. Selected case studies illustrate how specific donor‐acceptor combinations, conjugated linkages, metal centers, and pore microenvironments translate into enhanced performances through structure‐function correlations. Finally, we discuss remaining challenges in operational stability, scalable synthesis, structural precision, and target selectivity, and highlight emerging opportunities in data‐guided design, hybrid integration, and application‐oriented optimization of D‐A COFs for energy, environmental, and biomedical technologies.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning Reveals Design Rules for Thermal‐Mechanical Decoupling in Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal management materials face a persistent challenge: high thermal conductivity ( κ ) and low Young's modulus (E) are often mutually exclusive. Stiff materials typically conduct heat well while compliant materials tend to thermally insulate. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer exceptional structural tunability that breaks this trade‐off, yet a systematic understanding of κ ‐E decoupling remains elusive. Here we establish an interpretable machine learning framework integrating molecular simulations, six benchmarked models, and SHAP‐based feature analysis to screen over 52 000 topologically valid three‐dimensional COFs. Using random forest as the optimal model, we identify 26 COFs that simultaneously achieve high κ (> 0.8 W m − 1 K − 1 ) and low E (< 8 GPa), a combination difficult to attain by conventional design. SHAP analysis reveals that decoupling arises from nonlinear cooperative actions of multiple descriptors rather than single‐feature tuning. Phonon‐level transport analyses show that intermediate density, strong covalent connectivity, moderate porosity, and low linker fragment complexity balance volumetric heat capacity, phonon group velocity, and phonon lifetime, enabling high κ while preserving low E. This work provides a blueprint for thermally conductive yet mechanically compliant COFs and establishes a generalizable workflow for exploring property decoupling in framework materials.

title: Conjugation Continuity in Donor–Acceptor Crown Ether Covalent Organic Frameworks Boosts Photocatalytic Hydrogen Peroxide Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) production using covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is constrained by inefficient charge separation and discontinuous electron transport. While donor–acceptor (D–A) configurations can enhance internal electric fields, conjugation continuity within the acceptor moiety determines whether the separated charges can undergo long‐range migration to surface active sites,a factor often overlooked. Herein, we compare three crown‐ether (CE)‐based COFs: non‐D–A (CE‐BD‐COF), D–A non‐conjugated (CE‐BS‐COF), and D–A with a conjugation bypass (CE‐SA‐COF). CE‐BS‐COF exhibits a large dipole moment (8.92 D), but conjugation interruption localizes its LUMO, yielding a low surface photovoltage (34.0 mV). Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy reveals ultrafast initial charge transfer (τ 1 = 1.98 ps) and fast charge‐separation stabilization (τ 2 = 41.65 ps) in CE‐SA‐COF, together with a long‐lived charge‐separated state (>7 ns). Consequently, CE‐SA‐COF achieves a H 2 O 2 production rate of 2800.00 µmol g − 1 h − 1 under air in pure water, which is 3.5 times that of CE‐BD‐COF and 1.6 times that of CE‐BS‐COF. This work clarifies the distinct roles of D–A configuration and conjugation continuity, demonstrating that conjugation continuity, rather than polarization strength alone, governs electron transport to surface active sites and offering a design principle for COF photocatalysts.

title: Colloidally Prepared Homogeneous Wide-Bandgap Perovskites for Efficient Tandem Solar Cells with Industrial Silicon
abstract: Abstract Wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites, based on mixed halide-cation compositions, are widely employed as top cells in perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells to overcome the theoretical limitations of single-junction devices and exploit the full potential of crystalline silicon photovoltaics. However, uncontrolled nucleation rates and disordered crystallization kinetics in WBG perovskites pose a grave challenge to the preparation of phase-homogeneous perovskite films. Herein, we identify the undesirable precursor suspension as the main underlying reason for the compositional inhomogeneity and propose a colloidal engineering strategy to reconstruct the perovskite intermediate complex. According to classical colloidal theory and theoretical calculations, long-chain alkylphosphonic acid molecules are selected to precisely regulate colloidal structures and properties via their specific coordination strengths, leading to colloid-guided rapid nucleation and slow crystallization processes. Assisted by the uniform colloidal nucleation template, the prepared WBG perovskite films with compositional homogenization and reduced trap density enable tandem devices based on industrial silicon heterojunction cells to yield a champion power conversion efficiency of 34.01% (a certified reverse-scan PCE of 33.65%) for a 1 cm2 active area. The resultant encapsulated tandem device maintains 93% and 88% of its initial efficiency after 1211 h and 1000 h of one-sun operation at 25 and 65 °C, respectively, under their maximum power points.

title: Non‐Precious Metal High‐Entropy Oxide Sub‐1 nm Nanowires for Li‐O 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Highly active and structurally robust cathode catalysts are critically required to boost the electrochemical performance of lithium‐oxygen batteries (LOBs). Herein, a generally synthetic method of non‐precious metal high‐entropy oxide‐polyoxometalate sub‐1 nm nanowires (NPMHEO‐POM SNWs) has been successfully developed induced by POM clusters under mild solvothermal conditions. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations reveal that the dominantly driving forces for the assembly of POMs and multi‐metal oxides are the Coulomb and van der Waals forces, enabling precise theoretical guidance for targeted material synthesis. Benefiting from the 1D ultrafine structure with fully exposed active sites, the precise adjustment of components optimizing the adsorption capability of intermediate (LiO 2 *) and discharge product (Li 2 O 2 ), and the strong interactions of multi‐metal oxides and POMs contributing to the stability, the BiVZrNiCeO x ‐phosphomolybdic acid SNWs‐based LOB achieves a highly specific capacity of 9944 mAh g −1 and stable cycling durability for 312 cycles at 500 mA g −1 , highlighting their great promise as high‐efficiency electrocatalysts for advanced LOBs.

title: Colloidal Photonic Crystals Toward Scalable Manufacturing and Reliable Functions
abstract: ABSTRACT Colloidal photonic crystals (CPCs) have attracted considerable attention because of their specific optical properties and versatile structural functionality. While previous reviews have extensively covered the fundamental design and fabrication principles of functional CPCs, a systematic perspective on their transitioning from laboratory‐scale demonstrations to scalable manufacturing remains less explored. In this review, we therefore specifically fill this gap by summarizing recent advances on colloidal assembly, structural evolution, and stabilization strategies relevant to large‐scale fabrication and application‐oriented use. First, a concise overview of refining the classification of building blocks is provided for establishing a library to construct well‐defined periodic sophisticated photonic nanostructures. Second, we discuss scalable assembly from the perspective of processing constraints on how mild conditions, short assembly times, simplified procedures, and large‐area uniformity can be balanced. This is followed by discussing structural color modulation beyond stimulus‐based classification, and design strategies that enhance color fidelity, mechanical stability, and robustness. Emerging applications of these unique photonic systems, including anti‐counterfeiting, sensing, displays, and bio‐related devices, are highlighted. Finally, this review presents some challenges and perspectives on the development of colloid‐based scalable photonic materials, aiming to provide a scientific framework for bridging laboratory‐scale photonic materials with industrial‐scale manufacturing and reliable functions.

title: Spiral-in-Shrink Assembly of Microarchitected Circularly Polarized Luminescent Networks
abstract: Abstract High-fidelity three-dimensional displays require precise control over the polarization of light. Screens incorporating chiral emissive micropixels─which allow effective regulation of spin angular momentum─offer the potential for minimal-crosstalk, high-definition imaging. However, such highly asymmetric luminous, densely integrated microarrays have not yet been reported, owing to interfacial pinning effects and easy chiral structural degradation during miniaturization. Here, we present a spiral-in-shrink assembly strategy that couples evaporation-induced contraction with chiral self-organization in a nonequilibrium pathway. Geometry-confined shrinkage and chiral helically ordered microdomes act in concert to stabilize circularly polarized emission, yielding lateral features of 58 μm─corresponding to a significant improvement in miniaturization over reported dimensions. Large-area arrays comprising over 31,000 emissive units achieve 359 pixels per inch─and luminescence dissymmetry factors up to 1.25, enabling densely packed full-color photonic patterning. Moreover, spatially encoded handedness distributions underpin polarization-resolved mapping on aerial platforms for human–machine sensing. Our scalable route establishes a platform for cohesive chiroptical materials across advanced optical displays, polarization imaging, and intelligent sensing.

title: Reconstructing Colloidal NiO x Contacts for Efficient and Lamination‐Resilient Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐efficiency inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) increasingly rely on NiO x /self‐assembled monolayer (SAM) buried contacts, yet the geometric and surface heterogeneity of colloidal NiO x on textured fluorine‐doped tin oxide (FTO) compromises SAM assembly, perovskite crystallization, and interfacial strain uniformity. Here, β‐acryloyloxypropionic acid (CEA) is used to reconstruct both the mesoscale organization and exposed facets of NiO x . Through carboxyl anchoring and photoinduced interparticle coupling, CEA converts zero‐dimensional NiO x aggregates into chain‐connected assemblies that form conformal contacts while retaining colloidal processability. CEA also preferentially adsorbs on high‐energy NiO(111) facets, producing a NiO(100)‐dominated surface that promotes homogeneous SAM assembly. This coupled dimensional and facet reconstruction improves bottom‐interface crystallization, suppresses non‐radiative recombination and residual microstrain, and limits stress localization during BIPV‐grade lamination. The resulting PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.53% and a stabilized output of 27.52%, while 833.70 cm 2 modules deliver 20.85%. After lamination, semitransparent bifacial modules retain 98.98% and 99.56% of their initial front and rear‐side PCEs, respectively, and maintain 89% and 88% after 2400 h under ISOS‐L‐3 and ISOS‐D‐3 protocols. This work establishes molecularly reconstructed NiO x as a scalable interface for efficient and lamination‐resilient perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Drug‐Stiffened Polymer Worms: Allostery‐Inspired Activity Gating and Endogenous Enzyme‐Recharged Catalytic Cycling
abstract: ABSTRACT Natural enzymes achieve efficient and specific catalysis through precise allosteric regulation, a dynamic interplay of conformational rigidity and flexibility that remains largely unrealized in synthetic catalysts. Here, we report an allostery‐inspired polymer assembly whose catalytic and therapeutic functions are gated by programmable changes in supramolecular rigidity. The assemblies initially form flexible worm‐like micelles, whereas drug loading induces coordination‐driven crystallization into rigid nanorods. This rigidification restricts substrate accessibility and electron transfer, concurrently suppressing its peroxidase‐like activity, drug cytotoxicity, and fluorescence. In the glutathione (GSH)‐rich tumor microenvironment, disruption of metal coordination reverses rigidification, restores the flexible morphology, and reactivates all functions. The activated assemblies then use tumor‐overexpressed NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1) as an endogenous redox partner, channeling reducing equivalents from reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH) to replenish their electron reservoir and enable repeated catalytic turnover. This NQO1‐recharged cascade depletes intracellular GSH and NADH while generating cytotoxic hydroxyl radicals, thereby inducing apoptosis, ferroptosis, and cuproptosis, triggering immunogenic cell death, and eliciting robust antitumor immunity in vivo. By integrating allostery‐inspired structure gating with endogenous‐enzyme‐driven catalyst recharging, this work establishes an adaptive catalytic platform that addresses limitations in the activity regulation and redox cycling of artificial enzymes and offers a strategy for catalytic cancer therapy.

title: Spatial Electrostatic Complementarity in MOF Pores Enables Selective Recognition of Closely Related Fluoromethanes
abstract: ABSTRACT Trace purification of chemically similar gases is particularly challenging when molecular size and kinetics offer little contrast and conventional affinity descriptors provide conflicting guidance. Trifluoromethane (CHF 3 ) removal from monofluoromethane (CH 3 F) exemplifies this problem: CH 3 F has the greater dipole moment, and CHF 3 is more polarizable. Here, to our knowledge, we report the first adsorptive removal of trace CHF 3 from CH 3 F and demonstrate electrostatic complementary recognition (ECR) in interpenetrated anion‐pillared MOF pores. Localized, directional negative‐potential sites from TiF 6 2– pillars and surrounding electropositive pyridyl C─H domains complement the 1H/3F electrostatic pattern of CHF 3 while geometrically frustrating the inverse 3H/1F pattern of CH 3 F. All other benchmark adsorbents showed an overall preference for CH 3 F, whereas both TIFSIX frameworks achieved a reversal of adsorption preference toward CHF 3 under trace‐relevant conditions. TIFSIX‐Cu‐dpt, featuring a more focused and directional ECR environment, adsorbed 18.5 cm 3 /g of CHF 3 at 0.1 kPa. Neutron diffraction, adsorption thermodynamics, and molecular simulations support a spatially complementary multipoint binding mode. Fixed‐bed breakthrough of a binary feed containing 1000 ppm CHF 3 produced CH 3 F with >99.999% purity relative to CHF 3 at 320 L/kg. These results show how spatial electrostatic complementarity can translate subtle molecular differences beyond conventional scalar descriptors into selective adsorption.

title: Localized Geometric Frustration in One‐Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks for Photocoupled Electrocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocoupled electrocatalytic two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) offers a promising route to H 2 O 2 production, yet integrating photoinduced charge separation with bias‐driven interfacial electron transfer to enhance H 2 O 2 selectivity remains challenging. Here, we examine localized geometric frustration in a 1D benzothiazole‐based covalent organic framework (TDBT‐COF) as one structural feature associated with the 2e − pathway, using isoreticular naphthalene‐based TDNT‐COF and thiazolo[5,4‐d]thiazole‐based TDTT‐COF for comparison. The benzothiazole‐based monomer exhibits a 6.86° connection‐angle disparity that narrows to 1.38° in TDBT‐COF, reflecting partial accommodation by the periodic lattice. Under illumination, TDBT‐COF achieves 92% H 2 O 2 selectivity, exceeding those of TDNT‐COF (58%) and TDTT‐COF (66%) and its dark‐state selectivity (65%). During photocoupled electrocatalysis, TDBT‐COF delivers the H 2 O 2 production rate of 3.73 mol g −1 h −1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 91.9%. Theoretical calculations reveal greater electron transfer to adsorbed O 2 and lower *OOH formation barriers in TDBT‐COF than in the reference COFs. Photoexcitation further facilitates these interfacial processes. Locked‐relaxed fragment calculations give TDBT‐COF a larger strain energy and *OOH adsorption shift, in line with localized geometric frustration. This is the first study introducing the concept of localized geometric frustration to COF‐based photocoupled electrocatalysis, offering a structural perspective for catalyst design.

title: Late-Stage Fluorosulfurylation Using Sulfuryl Fluoride Bound within a Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: Abstract Organic S(VI) fluorides have garnered substantial interest for covalent drug discovery and chemoproteomics due to their ambient stability and unique electrophilic reactivity. Sulfuryl fluoride (SO2F2) is the ideal reagent for the synthesis of various S(VI)–F moieties, yet it is a toxic greenhouse gas, often making it incompatible with laboratory settings. Developing a strategy for handling SO2F2 that is amenable to high-throughput reaction discovery would enhance its utility in the laboratory without necessitating specialized equipment or extensive safety measures. Herein, we report a strategy to safely store reactive SO2F2 within a metal–organic framework (MOF) for its facile application to the synthesis of electrophilic, bioactive molecules. The solid SO2F2–Mg2(dobdc) reagent can be stored for at least five months with minimal gas loss due to the strong yet reversible interaction between SO2F2 and Mg2+ centers in the MOF, as confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Using this reagent, we prepare a range of drug-like arylfluorosulfates, primary and secondary acyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, saturated N-heterocyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, and N-heteroarene sulfamoyl fluorides, the last of which cannot be accessed using sulfonium salt alternatives to SO2F2 due to the requirement for strongly basic conditions. These findings represent the first experimental study of SO2F2 adsorption within a MOF and the first use of MOFs for late-stage fluorosulfurylation, paving the way toward a general approach to carefully handling dangerous, reactive gases as solid reagents.

title: Biomimetic Optically Encoded Hydrogel Fiber Enables Simultaneous Olfactory‐Mechanosensory Perception for Robotic Plume Tracing
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic odor plumes encode gas identity and airflow transport as coupled spatiotemporal cues, requiring olfactory‐mechanosensory fusion perception for intelligent robotic navigation in vision‐denied environments. Yet current olfactory‐mechanosensory systems typically rely on separated sensing units, limiting co‐localized mechanochemical discrimination. Here, we report a biomimetic flexible optical fiber (BFOF) comprising a coaxial hydrogel fiber with distributed, self‐assembled odor‐sensitive metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) on its exterior, enabling simultaneous decoding of wind vectors and olfactory cues within a single compact optical architecture. Inspired by the spatially integrated mechanoreceptors and chemoreceptors in ant antennae, the BFOF employs conformal MOF‐hydrogel interfaces to enhance evanescent‐field coupling without compromising receptor activity or waveguiding, partitioning multidimensional airflow attenuation and odor fluorescence into separable optical channels for low‐crosstalk olfactory‐mechanosensory fusion. Therefore, it achieves high sensitivity, fine directional selectivity, and fast temporal response across a wide range of airflow conditions. It identifies 16 individual gases, 96 mixtures, and the physiological states (unripe, ripe, overripe, and rotten) of 8 fruits with high accuracy. Coupled with a lightweight machine‐learning framework, this work establishes rapid, precise, and closed‐loop anemotactic navigation and multi‐target odor tracing in complex three‐dimensional (3D) spaces, offering a compact optical sensing platform for embodied robotic olfaction beyond static gas classification.

title: Chain‐Regulated Degradation of Polyvinyl Chloride in UiO‐Type Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Converting polyvinyl chloride (PVC) into valuable hydrocarbons is hindered by rapid dehydrochlorination, which produces mainly coke and HCl and limits global recycling to below 8%. Existing strategies activate specific bonds but overlook chain regulation. Here we show that regulating PVC chains within the sub‐nanometer channels of UiO‐type metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) redirects degradation from uncontrolled elimination to size‐selective chain scission. In Zr‐based UiO‐66 and UiO‐67, periodic acidic Zr clusters anchor PVC through Zr─Cl bonds, inducing heterolytic C─Cl cleavage and β‐scission of carbocationic intermediates. The yield of volatile hydrocarbons increases from <5 wt% for bulk PVC degradation to ∼30 wt% for degradation in the MOF. The aliphatic chain length is governed by the MOF geometry‐dictated anchoring spacing ( γ ): UiO‐66 ( γ = 8 C─C bonds) favours C9 hydrocarbons, whereas UiO‐67 ( γ = 10) favours C11 hydrocarbons. Molecular dynamics, thermodynamic calculations, and statistical kinetic modelling reveal that γ and carbocation‐mediated scission events control the carbon number of the products. This work establishes chain regulation as a design principle for controlling polymer degradation.

title: Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks@Bacterial Cellulose Mixed-Matrix Membranes for Pollution Elimination
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) represent promising porous photocatalytic candidates for water remediation, yet their practical deployment is severely hindered by their powdery nature, poor machinability, and limited recyclability. Herein, we report a facile in situ growth strategy to immobilize methyl-modified (HOF-101-CH3), fluorine-modified (HOF-101-F), and pristine HOF-101 nanocrystals within the three-dimensional interconnected nanofibrous network of bacterial cellulose (BC), yielding HOFs@BC mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs). Robust interfacial hydrogen bonding and physical cross-linking are constructed between HOF crystallites and BC nanofibers, which effectively suppress HOF aggregation, improve mechanical tolerance, and grant the composite membrane favorable hydrophilicity for aqueous-phase operation. Benefiting from the electron-donating methyl substituent, HOF-101-CH3-m delivers a more negative surface zeta potential (–28.8 mV), elevated charge-carrier separation efficiency, and superior dye-selective performance. It achieved a high selectivity ratio of 49.5 (permeation flux: 174 L m–2 h–1 bar–1) toward mixed cationic methylene blue (MB) and anionic methyl orange (MO), with 99.1% MB removal and merely 2% MO adsorption. After five separation-regeneration cycles, the membrane retains a selectivity ratio above 41.5 and maintains approximately 84% of its initial selectivity performance. Under visible-light irradiation, abundant reactive oxygen species (1O2, ·OH, and H2O2) are generated by the embedded HOF-101-CH3, endowing the membrane with photocatalytic self-cleaning capability. Notably, HOF-101-CH3-m achieves complete photodegradation of bisphenol A (BPA) within 50 min and maintains 95.3% degradation efficiency over five cyclic photocatalytic runs. This work demonstrates a feasible structural-engineering route to transform intractable powdery HOFs into mechanically robust multifunctional membranes, offering insights into the future design of HOF-derived functional materials toward integrated selective dye separation and photocatalytic elimination of organic water pollutants.

title: Multifunctional Conductive Nanoporous Carbon Honeycombs for Electrothermal Direct Air Capture
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct air capture (DAC) requires sorbent contactors that can process large air volumes with minimal pressure drop while enabling rapid, energy‐efficient regeneration. A multiscale conductive honeycomb contactor based on nanoporous amorphous carbon (NAC) is presented, in which adsorption‐active porosity, mechanical support, electrical conduction, and Joule‐heat generation are integrated within the same continuous framework. The fully interconnected NAC pore network accommodates epoxide‐functionalized polyethyleneimine while preserving CO 2 ‐accessible transport pathways after binder‐assisted shaping into a mechanically robust monolith. Straight‐through honeycomb channels enable low‐resistance airflow with efficient CO 2 capture, whereas the conductive NAC walls act as volumetric heating elements positioned directly adjacent to the CO 2 ‐binding phase for fast regeneration. The optimized contactor achieves a volumetric adsorption productivity of up to 0.32 mmol cm −3 h −1 while maintaining a specific fan‐energy demand below 10 J m −3 . Direct Joule heating enables more than 95% desorption within 16 min under the laboratory N 2 ‐purge protocol, approximately twofold faster than external heating under the same conditions, with no measurable capacity loss over a 15‐cycle short‐term test. The key advance is the simultaneous integration of high volumetric capacity, accessible nanoporous transport, mechanical robustness, low‐resistance airflow, and electrothermal regeneration within a single honeycomb contactor.

title: Synchronized Charge Transport and Mass Transfer via a Laser‐Programmed Spatial Interface Strategy for Scalable H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Synchronizing ultrafast charge transport with slower molecular mass transfer remains a central challenge for scalable H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Here, we introduce a laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy that patterns carbon nitride supported on a porous titanium mesh into adjacent pristine regions and dual‐defect microregions bearing cyano and nitrogen‐vacancy defects. Multiphysics simulations and potentiometric scanning electrochemical microscopy measurements suggest that this spatial architecture produces a localized potential response near the catalyst‐liquid interface, while in situ fluorescence microscopy indicates enhanced local O 2 availability. This coupled response is proposed to bridge the intrinsic timescale gap by facilitating directional extraction of photogenerated electrons while accelerating interfacial O 2 enrichment. The defect microregions promote proton‐coupled sequential two‐step O 2 reduction, whereas the conductive titanium mesh suppresses local electron accumulation and carbon nitride self‐photocorrosion. The optimized L‐CN/TM‐PS2 produces 2538 µmol L −1 g −1 H 2 O 2 within 120 min and achieves approximately 98.6% Escherichia coli inactivation. This work establishes the laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy as a design principle for synchronizing charge transport and mass transfer in supported photocatalysts for continuous‐flow environmental disinfection.

title: Cyclic Dimer Acceptor towards 20.9% Efficient Organic Solar Cells by Suppressing Electron‐Phonon Coupling
abstract: ABSTRACT Minimizing non‐radiative recombination energy loss (Δ E nr ) remains a critical challenge in boosting the efficiency of organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, we report a novel cyclic dimer acceptor, CR‐L8, rationally designed via an asymmetric linking strategy. In this molecular architecture, a thiophene linker extends the conjugated plane, while a flexible 1,6‐di(thiophen‐2‐yl)hexane chain acts as the another linker, synergistically modulating molecular conformation, packing, and aggregation. Compared to its linear analogues, the cyclic configuration significantly suppresses molecular vibrations and electron‐phonon coupling, leading to a substantially enhanced photoluminescence quantum yield and effective blockage of non‐radiative recombination channels. Importantly, CR‐L8‐based blend maintains favorable molecular packing and double‐fibril morphology, ensuring efficient charge transport. As a result, the D18:CR‐L8 device achieves a record efficiency of 17.23%, which is the highest value reported to date for OSCs employing cyclic dimer acceptor. Moreover, the Δ E nr of 0.155 eV in D18:CR‐L8 device is the lowest among OSCs with efficiencies exceeding 15%. Finally, incorporating CR‐L8 as the third component into D18:L8‐BO blend further boosts the performance, with the optimized ternary device achieving an impressive efficiency of 20.92%. This work pioneers a cyclic acceptor design strategy that mitigates non‐radiative recombination, offering a new molecular blueprint for high‐performance organic photovoltaics.

title: Boron‐Stabilized Diradicaloids of Chichibabin and Müller Hydrocarbons and Their Extended Analogues
abstract: ABSTRACT Boron incorporation provides an effective strategy for stabilizing organic open‐shell radicals while simultaneously modulating their electronic structures and properties. Herein, we report a series of boron‐containing Chichibabin‐ and Müller‐type diradicaloids featuring linearly extended π‐conjugated backbones and terminal triarylborane units. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that elongation of the conjugated bridges progressively weakens the interaction between two spin centers, leading to increased diradical character from 0.53 to 0.99, and narrowing the singlet–triplet energy gap from –3.42 to –2.58 kcal mol ‒1 . Despite their strong open‐shell nature, these organoboron diradicaloids exhibit remarkable stability, with half‐life time exceeding 40 days, owing to effective spin‐stabilization by the vacant p orbitals of the boron centers. They display backbone‐dependent aromaticity, tunable near‐infrared absorption, and reversible four‐electron redox behavior. Two‐electron chemical reduction affords the corresponding closed‐shell dianionic species with distinct aromatic reorganization and progressively red‐shifted fluorescence from 581 to 656 nm. These results thus establish a versatile boron‐based approach to stabilizing and tuning Chichibabin‐ and Müller‐type diradicaloids, providing new opportunities for the development of heterocyclic diradicaloid chemistry and functional open‐shell materials.

title: A Solution‐Processable Single‐Component Molecular Antiferromagnet
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing solution‐processable molecular materials with long‐range magnetic order remains a formidable challenge for molecular electronic and spintronic applications. Herein, we present a diethoxybenzene‐fused neutral‐radical gold dithiolene complex, Au(4OEt) , as a solution‐processable single‐component molecular antiferromagnet. Owing to its ethoxy substituents, Au(4OEt) adopts a two‐dimensional (2D) herringbone arrangement and exhibits semiconducting behavior characteristic of a Mott insulator. Magnetic susceptibility, solid‐state 1 H NMR, and magnetic torque measurements reveal the emergence of long‐range canted antiferromagnetic (CAF) order below approximately 8 K. Combined with transfer‐integral calculations and magnetic analyses, these results suggest that constructing a 2D herringbone arrangement of neutral‐radical molecules with dominant 2D exchange interactions (| J 2 | > | J 1 |) is important for stabilizing the magnetic ordering. Leveraging its solubility, we successfully fabricated solution‐processed crystalline thin films that retain the CAF phase. Moreover, the crystalline thin film functions as an ambipolar field‐effect transistor (FET). This work thus provides a remarkable example of a solution‐processable single‐component molecular antiferromagnet exhibiting ambipolar FET characteristics, and establishes a structural design strategy for realizing magnetically ordered crystalline thin films toward future antiferromagnetic devices.

title: Molecularly Programmed Stress Dissipation Strategy for Ultrastretchable Neuromorphic Electronics
abstract: ABSTRACT Intrinsically stretchable organic synaptic transistors (ISOSTs) using semiconducting polymers (SPs) hold promise for on‐body signal processing by mimicking biological synaptic functions and processing temporal bio‐signals directly at or near the point of data acquisition. However, conventional SPs designed primarily to increase polymer softness and mechanical compliance often lack molecular‐level mechanisms for effective stress dissipation, thereby limiting device‐level stretchability to below 100% and causing substantial degradation in electrical performance. Here, we demonstrate ISOSTs achieving 150% device‐level stretchability through molecularly programmed stress dissipation (MPSD) of an SP without incorporating soft segments into the backbone. This strategy promotes conformational flexibility and suppresses side‐chain interdigitation, enhancing chain dynamics and amplifying mechanical contrast between crystalline and amorphous domains. This facilitates localized stress accommodation and induces the formation of nano‐to‐micro scale crack clusters, termed artificial stretch marks (ASMs), which emulate the adaptive mechanical behavior of human skin. Leveraging this mechanism, ISOSTs maintain 83.8% of maximum current even under 150% strain while preserving synaptic behaviors. Furthermore, physical reservoir computing using the ISOSTs preserves electromyography classification performance under 150% tensile strain. This work presents a biomimetic stress dissipation strategy for intrinsically stretchable and stress‐adaptive neuromorphic electronics.

title: Dual‑Functionalized Mesoporous Bioactive Glass Integrating BMP‑2 and Apt19S for Outstanding MSC Recruitment and Osteogenesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Insufficient osteoinductive capacity and deficient mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) remain major challenges for artificial bone materials in treating critical‐sized bone defects. To alleviate these limitations, we engineered mesoporous bioactive glass (MBG) nanoparticles with superior osteogenic activity via loading of bone morphogenetic protein‐2 (BMP‐2) and exceptional MSC recruitment capacity by covalent grafting of nucleic acid aptamer Apt19S. The BMP‐2‐immobilized MBG (MBG‐BMP‐2) exhibited sustained release of BMP‐2, primarily attributed to the confinement effects of size‐matched mesopores. The Apt19S‐modified MBG (MBG‐Apt19S) effectively recruited bone marrow MSCs (BMSCs) in vitro and efficiently promoted migration of targeted MSCs in vivo. MBG‐BMP‐2 effectively promoted osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs in vitro and enhanced new bone formation in a rat cranial defect model. In contrast, while MBG‐Apt19S showed less direct osteogenic stimulation to BMSCs in vitro, it elicited a substantially greater bone regeneration response in vivo, outperforming even MBG‐BMP‐2. Notably, MBG co‐immobilized with BMP‐2 and Apt19S (MBG‐BA) produced the most robust osteogenic outcomes. Mechanistically, this superior performance was ascribed to the concurrent activation of the Smad1/5/8 and ERK1/2 signaling axes. This study elucidates the outstanding effects of osteoinductivity and MSC recruitment by MBG‐BA, which could offer valuable insights for the development of multifunctional artificial bone materials.

title: Dancing with Nitro Groups: Synthesis and Structures of Fully Nitrated Compounds
abstract: Conspectus Full nitration increases oxygen content but also intensifies electron withdrawal, steric congestion, and electrostatic repulsion, making further substitution difficult and often reducing chemical or thermal stability. Fully nitrated compounds are therefore more than candidate oxidizers or explosives. They provide demanding molecular models for understanding how multiple strongly electron-withdrawing groups reshape reactivity, bond polarization, molecular geometry, and crystal packing. Their stability is also multidimensional. A compound may resist thermal decomposition yet remain susceptible to water, moist air, or light, making chemical robustness as important as decomposition temperature and mechanical sensitivity. For the purposes of this Account, fully nitrated compounds are molecular scaffolds in which all substitutable positions of the parent framework are occupied by nitro or nitro-bearing functionalities. Locally edited derivatives and ionic assemblies are discussed as related polynitro systems. At the molecular level, alternating nitro and nitroamino groups introduce hydrogen-bond donors and modify electron delocalization. TNTNB thereby achieves markedly improved resistance to water, acids, and bases relative to hexanitrobenzene, whereas DNTP illustrates how the same substitution concept can increase packing efficiency and crystal density, albeit with a thermal-stability penalty. Studies of octanitropyrazoles and decanitrobipyrazoles further show that the attainable degree of nitration cannot be described by a universal numerical ceiling. Substitution sequence, relative positions, and backbone geometry determine whether densely nitrated groups can be accommodated. These principles culminated in BITE-202, a bitriazole carrying 12 nitro groups that shows no detectable changes after 180 days in water and decomposes at 164 °C. Its behavior is consistent with greater separation of neighboring substituents, a planar conjugated backbone, and a more uniform electrostatic-potential distribution. Full nitration can also provide a platform for functions beyond maximizing oxygen content. Using fused BITE-203 as a stable reference scaffold, replacement of one ring-bound nitro group by an azide produced the azide-edited fused derivative FTT and introduced a locally distinct electrostatic region. Initiation experiments, rather than calculated energetic parameters alone, established the resulting functional change: β-FTT initiated cyclotrimethylenetrinitramine (RDX) with a reported minimum primary charge of 30 mg, whereas BITE-203 did not under the same conditions. Stabilization can then be extended beyond covalent structure into the lattice. Hydrogen-bonded frameworks encapsulate nitroformate, cationic metal–organic frameworks immobilize dinitramide or polynitroazolate counterions, and polynitro frameworks invert the conventional host–guest relationship. In the latter systems, an octanitro anionic framework adapts to incorporate hydrazinium and neutral hydrazine, retaining the neutral guest until framework decomposition and creating a self-redox energetic lattice. Together, these results establish a hierarchical design principle: the properties of fully nitrated compounds depend not only on how many nitro groups are present but also on where they are placed, how their electronic effects are distributed, and what role they assume in the crystal lattice. Remaining challenges include the apparent density plateau of many neutral fully nitrated crystals, limited formulation-compatibility and aging data, and the need for scalable synthesis. Future progress will increasingly rely on crystal engineering and multicomponent assembly to coordinate energetic, stabilizing, and functional roles that a single molecule cannot readily satisfy.

title: Turning on Circularly Polarized Afterglow via Coordination Assembly
abstract: ABSTRACT Materials exhibiting circularly polarized afterglow (CPA) properties have garnered significant attention due to their promising applications in information storage and anti‐counterfeiting. However, achieving CPA signals in luminescent materials from “off” to “on” while simultaneously enhancing phosphorescence quantum yield (Φ Phos. ) remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a synergistic assembly strategy that integrates rigid boric oxide (B 2 O 3 ) matrix encapsulation with metal coordination to enable the generation of CPA from non‐CPA materials and synergistically boost Φ Phos . A series of axially chiral molecules were reported, incorporating binaphthyl as the chiral source and phenanthroline as the coordination unit. Encapsulation of these molecules in B 2 O 3 produced yellow afterglow with a lifetime of 1.02 s, but no CPA was observed. After the iridium center coordinated to the phenanthroline unit and the resulting assemblies were encapsulated in B 2 O 3 , the metal‐organic assemblies not only retained the long‐afterglow property but also exhibited a distinct CPA signal. Concurrently, the Φ Phos. significantly increased from 6.7% to 26.4%. This work shows that combining rigid B 2 O 3 encapsulation with metal coordination assembly confers CPA properties and tunable emission, offering a new route to high‐performance CPA materials.

title: A Generic and High‐Throughput Capillary‐Driven Shear Assembly for Fabrication of Highly Aligned Nanomaterials
abstract: ABSTRACT Assembling two‐dimensional (2D) nanomaterials into macroscopic architectures that retain their exceptional intrinsic properties is pivotal for next‐generation functional devices. However, a persistent trade‐off remains between structural precision and fabrication throughput: scalable techniques often succumb to Brownian‐induced orientation relaxation, yielding loosely packed, isotropic networks, while precision‐oriented methods lack industrial scalability. Herein, we demonstrate a capillary‐driven shear assembly (CDSA) strategy—a continuous, hydrodynamically driven approach that leverages the synergy of capillary pressure and fluid dynamics to fabricate highly aligned, densified nanocomposites. Unlike conventional strategies, the CDSA strategy utilizes capillary forces generated by porous media to create a confined horizontal shear flow, which aligns the nanosheets horizontally at the interface. This strategy not only boosts assembly speed, but also proves universally applicable to a diverse library of 2D materials, including graphene oxide (GO), MXene, MoS 2 , and h‐BN. Importantly, after graphitization treatments, g‐CDSA‐GO exhibits a high in‐plane thermal conductivity. Further incorporation of polyimide‐derived graphitic bridges increases the through‐plane thermal conductivity to 21.3 W m −1 K −1 while maintaining an in‐plane value of 1406 W m −1 K −1 . These results establish CDSA as a scalable route for constructing highly ordered 2D architectures.

title: Two-dimensional phthalocyanine-based conjugated covalent organic frameworks: Progress in structures, properties, and applications
abstract: Two-dimensional phthalocyanine-based covalent organic frameworks (2D Pc-COFs) synergistically combine the intrinsic photoelectric behavior and M–N4 catalytic centers of phthalocyanine macrocycles with COF advantages, including crystalline porous channels, large specific surface area, and molecularly designable frameworks, enabling broad use in electrocatalysis, photocatalysis, energy conversion and storage, sensing, and biomedicine. Departing from conventional classification schemes based on bonding modes or application fields, this review adopts electron delocalization pathways as the core criterion, dividing 2D Pc-COFs into fully π-conjugated and p–π conjugated systems. This framework encompasses 13 representative linkage types and covers key research advances since the first report of Pc-COFs. Fully π-conjugated systems feature continuous in-plane sp2 π-electron networks that facilitate efficient charge transport, making them well suited for charge-transfer-dominated applications. In contrast, p–π conjugated systems achieve superior chemical stability and enhanced functional tunability through heteroatom-mediated electronic coupling, which enables precise modulation of the active-site microenvironment and reaction selectivity. Furthermore, this review systematically compares their structural features, electronic properties, synthetic strategies, and functional performances, elucidates the underlying structure–property relationships, and outlines current challenges and future research directions. Collectively, this work provides systematic theoretical guidance for the rational design and functional expansion of high-performance Pc-COF materials.

title: Sub‐Kilogram‐Scale Synthesis of High‐Quality Upconversion Nanoparticles
abstract: ABSTRACT Lanthanide‐doped upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) have attracted significant interest for applications in nanophotonics, biomedicine, and life sciences. However, the lack of stable, high‐quality, and scalable synthetic methods remains a major obstacle to their industrial deployment. Herein, a modified solid‐liquid thermal decomposition (SLTD) strategy is proposed using self‐prepared anhydrous rare‐earth (RE) acetates, together with solid NaHF 2 powder as both the fluorine and sodium sources. Rapid thermal decomposition of NaHF 2 at the solid‐liquid interface enables controlled nucleation and growth, allowing precise synthesis of NaYF 4 :Yb/Er UCNPs with tunable morphologies and sizes. Remarkably, this approach achieves a record‐breaking sub‐kilogram‐scale synthesis in a single batch with high yield (>94%) and excellent reproducibility. By adjusting the solvent composition or introducing Gd 3+ dopants, the particle morphologies can be tailored from rod‐like to disk‐like and spherical, with sizes ranging from 30 to 130 nm. This strategy is further applicable to other NaREF 4 hosts and core‐shell nanostructures. Benefiting from the low‐hydroxyl reaction conditions and high crystallinity, the resulting UCNPs exhibit an upconversion quantum yield approximately 30 times higher than those produced by conventional co‐precipitation methods, exceeding 10% for Er 3+ ‐activated core‐shell nanocrystals. Their practical utility is demonstrated in PDMS‐based flexible optical fiber temperature sensing with excellent sensitivity and stability.

title: Bioinspired Architected Materials for Aging‐Competent Brain Organoids: Multiscale Design, Assembly, and Translation
abstract: ABSTRACT Human brain organoids provide models of neural development and disease, but their developmentally young state and incompletely organized microenvironment limit the reconstruction of late‐life neural tissue. This review frames aging‐competent brain organoids as biohybrid architected systems in which cellular composition, extracellular matrices, material interfaces, transport pathways, and sensing or actuation modules are organized across length scales. An architecture–property–exposure–function framework is developed to connect matrix mechanics and ligand presentation, bioelectronic interfaces, vascular and oxygen‐regulating systems, redox‐active materials, programmable carriers, and nanosensors with tissue responses. Aging competence is defined as the capacity of a mature organoid to undergo reproducible, cell‐type‐resolved age‐associated transitions and to exhibit a progressive loss of homeostatic reserve after calibrated challenge. Accordingly, material‐enabled phenotypes are evaluated through molecular age, organelle flux, neurovascular and immune states, network performance, and challenge–recovery behavior, while excluding hypoxia, necrosis, acute toxicity, and material persistence as dominant explanations. The resulting design logic links multiscale assembly and multifunctionality to disease‐matched models of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis/frontotemporal degeneration, and Huntington's disease, as well as to nanomedicine screening and translational qualification. Treating the organoid–material construct as an integrated architecture establishes functional materials as controllable modules for building, perturbing, monitoring, and therapeutically interrogating human brain aging.

title: Ultrahigh Energy Storage in Supramolecular Biomass‐Based Dielectrics
abstract: ABSTRACT Biomass‐based polymer dielectrics exhibit considerable potential for sustainable capacitive energy storage applications. However, they are limited by a relatively small discharged energy density (<20 J cm −3 ) with low efficiency compared to their state‐of‐the‐art petroleum‐derived counterparts. Herein, a green supramolecular architecture design is implemented by introducing poly (arylene ether urea) (PEEU) into a cyanoethyl cellulose (CEC) matrix. Hydrogen‐bond‐mediated PEEU supramolecular association is integrated with micrometer‐scale PEEU‐rich microdomains and abundant CEC/PEEU interfacial regions, collectively promoting structural densification and suppressing charge migration. Consequently, our supramolecular dielectric composites exhibit a remarkable breakdown strength of 758 MV m −1 and a superior discharged energy density of 36.4 J cm −3 with an efficiency of 76.9%, well surpassing currently existing biomass‐based counterparts. This work provides a rational supramolecular assembly framework to fabricate environmentally sustainable dielectrics featuring outstanding room‐temperature energy‐storage performance and self‐cealing capability for next‐generation capacitors.

title: A Series of TTDO-Based Energetic Cocrystals: From Supramolecular Assembly and Structural Analysis to Energetic Performance and Combustion Modulation
abstract: Abstract The inherent trade-off between high energy output and safety remains a critical bottleneck in the development of advanced propellants and high-energy-density materials. Here, we present a supramolecular assembly strategy using 2,4,6-triamino-1,3,5-triazine-1,3-dioxide (TTDO) as a Lewis base host to construct energetic cocrystals. Guided by COSMO screening, five nitro-containing Lewis acid energetic molecules were successfully cocrystallized with TTDO. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals diverse protonation behaviors and extensive hydrogen-bonding networks, while electrostatic potential analysis shows that the positions of electrostatic potential extrema shift upon cocrystallization, correlating with significantly reduced mechanical sensitivity. Notably, TTDO-LLM-116 and TTDO-NMTT serve as multifunctional additives in ammonium perchlorate (AP)-based composite propellants. Incorporating only 10 wt % of these cocrystals merges the two-stage decomposition of AP into a single exothermic event and reduces the decomposition activation energy from 250.2 kJ·mol–1 to 107.4 kJ·mol–1 and 63.3 kJ·mol–1. Laser ignition experiments confirm enhanced combustion with a substantially shorter duration. As combustion additives, these cocrystals reduce the activation energy of AP while avoiding the energy-dilution effect commonly encountered with inert metal oxide catalysts. This work establishes TTDO-based cocrystals as a versatile platform for developing low-sensitivity, high-performance energetic materials, and advanced combustion modifiers for propellant applications.

title: Sublevel-selective electron spin hyperpolarization of triplet radical pairs in metal–organic frameworks
abstract: Molecular spin systems are promising platforms for spin-based technologies because their electronic structures can be synthetically tailored and integrated into higher-order assemblies. Photogenerated radical pairs can exhibit spin hyperpolarization under ambient conditions, yet extending such spin dynamics from isolated molecules to structurally organized materials remains challenging. Here, we report a metal–organic framework that regulates the generation of spin-polarized radical pairs within locally well-defined donor–acceptor arrangements. N,N’-di(4-pyridyl)−1,4,5,8-naphthalenetetracarboxdiimide is introduced into a zinc tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin-based framework. Dense donor–acceptor packing promotes efficient quenching of the porphyrin singlet excited state and selectively forms strongly coupled triplet radical pairs polarized in the zero-spin projection sublevel. These radical pairs exhibit narrow electron paramagnetic resonance signals and long spin-lattice relaxation times. Their spin-lattice relaxation dynamics persist in various guest solvents and vary with guest identity, demonstrating a route to chemically responsive spin materials based on porous, locally organized donor–acceptor frameworks. While molecular spin systems are promising platforms for spin-based technologies, previous studies have mainly focused on isolated molecular systems embedded in dense solid matrices. Here, the authors report a metal-organic framework approach for regulating the generation of spin-polarized radical pairs within a well-defined donor-acceptor arrangement.

title: Precise Interlayer Ru─O─M Electronic Bridge Installation in Hydrotalcite‐Like Metal‐Organic Frameworks for Boosted Electrochemical Amine Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical oxidation of amines provides an energy‐efficient route to value‐added nitriles, yet controlling sequential dehydrogenation and intermediate conversion at defined active sites remains challenging. Herein, framework‐anchored Ru─O─M (M = CoNi) electronic bridges are constructed in hydrotalcite‐like CoNi‐DABCO through a controllable sulfate‐to‐hydroxide anion‐substitution strategy. The generated hydroxyl‐rich interlayer sites enable site‐specific anchoring and condensation of Ru species, producing highly dispersed RuO x domains chemically coupled to the CoNi framework. These bridges induce interfacial charge redistribution and regulate imine intermediate conversion during amine electrooxidation. The optimized Ru 9% @CoNi‐DABCO achieves a benzylamine oxidation onset potential of 1.24 V vs RHE and 95% Faradaic efficiency toward benzonitrile, while maintaining efficiencies of 83–95% toward representative primary amines. In situ infrared spectroscopy reveals reduced accumulation of imine‐related intermediates and a 0.17 V cathodic shift in the extrapolated spectroscopic onset of the * C≡N signal, consistent with more favorable benzonitrile formation. Density functional theory calculations show that the Ru─O─M interface lowers the reaction free energy of imine‐related dehydrogenation by 0.538 eV at 1.45 V vs RHE and facilitates product release. This work establishes anion substitution as an effective strategy for constructing site‐confined metal motifs in MOFs to regulate multistep organic electrocatalytic dehydrogenation.

title: Swarm-inspired magnetic metal-organic framework-based microbots for on-demand moisture manipulation
abstract: Hygroscopic metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising candidates for atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) and humidity control. Nevertheless, their practical application is often hindered by the poor manipulability of inherent powder forms and mass transfer limitations caused by the shaping. Drawing inspiration from the “hot defensive ball” aggregation morphology of honeybee swarms, a versatile magnetic shaping strategy hereby was reported to assemble MOF-based microbots, which enhances the formability of MOF powders. The obtained magnetic hygroscopic MOF (mMOF-303) exhibits enhanced water adsorption kinetics and enables efficient regeneration via multimodal heating strategies, including photothermal, electrothermal, and magnetothermal heating. Besides, the magnetic MOF-based microbots can change their aggregation patterns and perform directional motion according to application scenarios, enabling rapid water vapor sorption-desorption rates and precision confined space humidity control. This work provides a universal strategy to impart versatile formability to static MOF powders, paving the way for MOF engineering and advanced moisture management.

title: Raman-Inactive Metal–Organic Framework Nanoribbons as Plasmonic-Nanocavity Spacers and Molecular Trappers for SERS Detection
abstract: Abstract The integration of plasmonic nanostructures with metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) has emerged as a powerful strategy to enhance the sensitivity and selectivity of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS). While the resultant hybrid systems exploit localized surface plasmon resonance for electric-field enhancement and MOF porosity for molecular enrichment, their practical applications are hindered by challenges, including intrinsic Raman interference from MOFs, precise control over MOF dimensions, and restricted plasmon coupling configurations. Herein we present a promising design featuring Raman-inactive MOF nanoribbons embedded within plasmonic nanogaps between a gold film and gold nanospheres (NSs). The sub-10 nm MOF interlayer eliminates Raman background while maximizing electromagnetic enhancement. The resultant Au-film/MOF/NSs architecture enables remarkable SERS performances with enhancement factors of 1010 across diverse molecular sizes. This work not only enriches the toolbox of MOF-based plasmonic sensing platforms, but also opens the way for further exploration into other Raman-inactive MOFs and mechanisms.

title: Janus Vapor‐Gap Membrane Coupling Superhydrophobic Evaporation and Superhydrophilic Condensation for Pressure‐Driven Desalination
abstract: ABSTRACT Pressure‐driven distillation (PD) has emerged as a transformative technology for harnessing non‐conventional water resources, leveraging hydraulic pressure to accelerate vapor generation and transport across vapor‐gap membranes. Despite its promise, the paradigm of conventional PD is fundamentally constrained by overlooked thermodynamic energy barrier, which severely limits overall process efficiency. Herein, we report the first conceptualization and fabrication of an ultra‐selective Janus vapor‐gap membrane engineered explicitly for PD, featuring a superhydrophilic, highly crystalline, and defect‐free covalent organic framework (COF) layer that decisively overcomes this limitation. The Janus membrane embodies a bilayered architecture with the upper layer functions as a vapor generation zone, sustaining a robust gas‐liquid interface for efficient evaporation, while the lower layer serves as a confined condensation zone that significantly reduces the energy barrier for vapor‐to‐liquid phase transition. This strategic spatial decoupling of evaporation and condensation enables a synergistic enhancement of the entire PD process. The resulting Janus membrane achieves near‐complete rejections of nonvolatile solutes. In practical desalination scenarios, it demonstrates outstanding anti‐fouling and chlorine resistance. This work not only highlights the potential of crystalline porous materials in PD technology, but also provides a pathway for architected Janus membranes that transcend the efficiency limits of conventional desalination processes.
